title: Signed extension as a module cochain map
statement: Let $X',T'$ be schemes and $f':X'\to T'$ a morphism. Let $M$ be a module sheaf on $X'$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $W_i$, $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, any finite family of opens. Let $K$ be an integer cochain complex of module sheaves on $T'$ with zero negative terms. Suppose for all nonnegative $p$ and opens $B\subset T'$ there are additive equivalences $a_{p,B}:\Gamma(B,K^p)\simeq\prod_t\Gamma((\bigcap_lW_{t(l)})\cap(f')^{-1}B,M)$ indexed by increasing $(p+1)$-tuples [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. Assume these equivalences commute with restrictions of $B$, take multiplication by $b\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_{T'})$ to multiplication by the restriction of $(f')^*b$ on each coordinate, and intertwine $d_K$ with the signed face-restriction sum. Let $D$ be a nonnegative cochain complex of module sheaves on $X'$. Suppose its terms, after forgetting to presheaves of global-ring modules, are identified by natural isomorphisms $e_p$ with the usual all-tuple Cech terms of $W,M$. Assume $e$ intertwines differentials, and each coordinate on an open $C\subset X'$ takes multiplication by $b\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_{X'})$ to multiplication by its restriction to $(\bigcap_lW_{y(l)})\cap C$. Let $L=(f'_*D)^{\mathrm{ext}}$ and let $q$ be its ordered coordinate maps [def-pc-ordered-cech-module-coordinates]. There is a cochain map $I:K\to L$ of module sheaves such that $q_{p,B,t}(I(s))=a_{p,B,t}(s)$ for every nonnegative degree $p$, base open $B$, section $s$ of $K^p$ and increasing tuple $t$. No restriction map or retraction identity is asserted.

proof.text: Define a private full-tuple signed value by summing over permutations whose reordered underlying Fin r tuple is strictly increasing. Each summand is the sign times coefficient restriction from the ordered intersection to the full product times the inverse image of the base open. Repeated tuples have no contributing permutation. On an increasing tuple only the identity permutation contributes: Tuple.unique_monotone and injectivity show uniqueness. Its sign is one, and the composite of the full-product-to-intersection and intersection-to-product arrows is the identity in the poset of opens. This proves the increasing-coordinate identity in Lean.

Evaluate the presentation e_p on an open C. Compose its evaluation with PreservesProduct.iso for evaluation and ModuleCat.piIsoPi to obtain an actual additive equivalence V between sections of D^p on C and all full-tuple coordinates. The identities piIsoPi_hom_ker_subtype and piComparison_comp_π identify V with the coordinate maps. Apply V inverse to the full signed formula of a_{p,B}(s). This defines additive section maps v_{p,B}. Naturality of e followed by each projection, hn and functoriality of coefficient restriction show that v commutes with restrictions; the two composite arrows between opens are equal by thinness. Apply V and each coordinate to scalar multiplication: hlinear describes the output scalar, hl describes the input scalar, map_smul transports it, and integer signs commute with local scalars. Finite sums preserve these identities. PresheafOfModules.homMk assembles these explicit maps into module-sheaf morphisms, and the inverse extendXIso gives the graded maps to the extended pushforward. No postponed existence theorem supplies any data.

On a base open B use the SiteCechComplex whose p-tuple open is (infimum_l W_{t(l)}) intersect f inverse B. Its universal arrows and the canonical map to the categorical product times f inverse B are actual homOfLE maps; the latter is an isomorphism by the product projections. Use orderedCechNaturalCoordinate from the proved degreewise-projection module only as a full-coordinate definition. Transport its values to this intersection model. The filtered-permutation sum equals signedCechExtension: for an injective tuple there is exactly one strictly increasing permutation, its sorting permutation; for a noninjective tuple every summand vanishes. This identifies the full coordinates of the graded maps with the sectionwise signed extension.

Compose hd with the full-tuple projection and evaluate on a section. The proved upstream TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplexFunctor_d_π in WeilConjectures.Topology.Sheaves.CechComparison expands the categorical differential as the alternating sum of signed face restrictions. Transporting to the intersection model gives SiteCechComplex.differentialValue: additivity moves restrictions through the finite sum and integer coefficients, and the restriction composites agree by uniqueness of arrows of opens. Apply signedCechExtension_differential. On each increasing tuple every face is increasing, so signedCechExtension_increasing followed by ha identifies the ordered differential coordinates with a applied to d_K. Thus all full coordinates of the two adjacent composites agree. Injectivity of the product-intersection isomorphisms, the product projections, e and extendXIso proves their equality as module-sheaf morphisms. HomologicalComplex.extend_d_eq handles the differential transport.

Define the integer-degree components by the graded maps, transported along Int.toNat_of_nonneg, for nonnegative integers, and zero otherwise. For an adjacent pair beginning in a nonnegative degree, Int.eq_ofNat_of_zero_le reduces the chain condition to the proved adjacent equation. If the source degree is negative, hK gives IsZero of that term, so eq_of_src proves the chain condition, including degree minus one to zero. The increasing-coordinate calculation from the first step proves the required formula. The public theorem signature and all hypotheses remain unchanged.
